strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - os: ubuntu-latest
            runner: ubuntu-latest
          - os: macos-m5
            runner: [self-hosted, macos-m5]
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@2286a0c042b44434fe26d292bbce8d34f7ec662b # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get
      - uses: ./.github/actions/sqlite3-native-assets-prewarm
      - name: Install the curl|sh dialects (dash + busybox)
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends dash busybox
          dash -c 'echo dash: $(dash -c "echo ok")'
          busybox echo busybox: ok
      - name: UT — template lint + golden drift (AC1/AC6)
        run: dart test test/site/setup_sh_portability_test.dart test/site/installer_golden_test.dart
      - name: IT — piped wizard under dash/busybox/bash (AC2-AC5)
        run: dart test test/integration/setup_wizard_portability_test.dart

  # Issue #675: the suite must be immune to a hostile ambient env — the
  # dmtools ai-teammate runner exports FA_PROVIDER_TYPE / FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG /
  # FAH_PROVIDER, which used to decide test fate through the args resolver.
  # Run the non-integration suite under the same hostile env so any
  # ambient-env read that leaks back into resolution regresses loudly.
  # gh-1198 rework: the runner now ALSO exports FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE (the
  # provider-queue env won over the file queue and silently flipped the
  # /providers queue editor tests to the env-wins refusal on the PR head) —
  # the var rides the same hostile block so a future ambient read of it
  # regresses here, not only on the runner.
  hostile-env:
    name: Hostile ambient env
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read
    env:
      FA_PROVIDER_TYPE: zai
      FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG: '{"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"glm-5.3-flash","apiKeyEnvVar":"ZAI_CODE_KEY"}'
      FAH_PROVIDER: zai
      FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE: '[{"provider_type":"zai","provider_config":{"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"glm-5.3-flash","apiKeyEnv":"ZAI_CODE_KEY"}}]'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@2286a0c042b44434fe26d292bbce8d34f7ec662b # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - uses: ./.github/actions/sqlite3-native-assets-prewarm
      - name: dart test under hostile ambient env
        run: dart test --exclude-tags integration

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Nightly parity (2026-09-23): the two legs that stayed nightly-only went
  # red on main night after night before anyone looked — the CLI-coverage
  # ratchet (12.07% < 12.17%) and the Terminal-visual PTY suite (five
  # regressions, several cascading out of fixed-port collisions). Both legs
  # are part of the COMMON PR suite: they run on every CI invocation (the
  # Machine SM dispatches ci.yml per PR head), unconditioned by path — a
  # diff that breaks them must red-block THE PR, never the 3:30 nightly.
  # gh-1538: nightly is builds + integration-only now — this PR leg IS the
  # only Terminal-visual run (the nightly cli-visual duplicate is retired).
  # gh-1537 retired the post-merge main CI run, so this pre-merge leg is
  # the only Terminal-visual gate any tree ever sees; nightly's remaining
  # legs are a scheduled backstop, not a second merge gate.
  # gh-1300 (2026-10-06): the PTY/CLI shards pay toolchain+boot ONCE per
  # run, not per test. Every integration test spawns a fresh CLI; JIT
  # `dart bin/fah.dart` cost VM start + CFE kernel compile ~30 s PER SPAWN
  # on loaded ARM runners (the dominant term: 29 files, 3 shards x
  # ~350 s). This job compiles the AOT bundle once, the shards download
  # it and point the FA_BIN seam (test/integration/pty_harness.dart,
  # faCliCommand) at it — spawn ~1 s, per-test isolation untouched (each
  # spawn is still a fresh process with its own env/cwd). The binary MUST
  # match the PR's sources: built fresh in this run, never cached across
  # runs; the shards fail loudly if it is missing or dead (`test -x` +
  # `--version` smoke), never silently fall back to JIT.
  fa-aot-build:
    name: AOT fa binary (compiled once per run, gh-1300)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@2286a0c042b44434fe26d292bbce8d34f7ec662b # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      # Same hooks cache key as the shards: the build pays the native

# Root Cause Analysis — gh-2430 `[ci-red] v1.0.779 failed`

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: The v1.0.779 CI run went red on three jobs — `Hostile ambient env`, `Quality gate`, `Advance vpinned marker` — all traced to ONE test failure: `test/cli/agent_cli_waiting_fast_settle_test.dart` AC1 failed in its teardown with `FileSystemException: Deletion failed, path = '/tmp/fah2275-ac1-GCUXOM' (OS Error: Directory not empty, errno = 39)` (15298 passed, 1 failed, run 45696875652, job 139498238453).

**Root cause**: `settleCli()` in `test/cli/agent_cli_waiting_fast_settle_test.dart` fabricates adopted background jobs with fake pids (4242/4243) via `ShellJobRegistry.adoptRunningEntry` but pins only the WAITING layer's process probe (`cli.waitingProcessTableForTest`). It leaves the registry's adopted-liveness poll (`ShellJobRegistry._adoptedPoll`, a 5-second wall-clock `Timer` armed by `_adopt` at `lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart:747-755`) pointed at the REAL `ps` probe (`_probeLivenessTable`, no `livenessTableOverride`). The timer always fires AFTER the test body ends (body ≈ 110 ms, tick at 5 s). Because real hosts have no pid 4242, `refresh()` (`_AdoptedShellJob.refresh`, `shell_jobs.dart:1132`) judges the fabricated job dead → `_markGone` → `AgentCliShellJobSettle._onShellJobSettled` → `unawaited(_waiting.jobSettled(job))` (`agent_cli_waiting.dart:1337`) → `_manifestRemove` → `_withRegistryLock` → `createDir('<tmp workspace>/.fah/bash_jobs')` + atomic rewrite of `running.json` — a file write into the temp workspace after the test completed. Under CI load that write lands INSIDE the teardown `workspace.delete(recursive: true)` walk → the final rmdir sees a fresh entry → `Directory not empty, errno = 39`. Outside the delete window the same write silently resurrects the deleted temp dir in `/tmp`.

The other two red jobs are pure cascades:
- `Quality gate` (job 139538620905): aggregate verdict `hostile-env = failure` → `Quality gate FAILED: a leg is failure (hostile-env)`.
- `Advance vpinned marker` (job 139538678185): `pin_release.sh v1.0.779` → `E_PIN_PROVENANCE_MISSING` — the release published no `SHA256SUMS` because publish is gated on the Quality gate's `dart_ok`, which the hostile-env red flipped. No independent defect.

**Impact**: Flaky CI red on any leg that runs the file (hostile-env was the unlucky one; core-test shards got lucky — the tick's write usually lands after their deletes and merely leaks `/tmp` garbage on ephemeral runners). Same latent hazard exists in the sibling `agent_cli_waiting_manifest_lock_test.dart` fixture (identical fabricated-pid adoption + raw recursive delete; that file was previously hardened with a `_deleteBestEffort` retry but NOT pinned — left untouched here, noted for follow-up).

**Fix approach**: Test-only. Pin the registry poll table for the fabricated pids, following the established pattern in `test/cli/agent_cli_waiting_integration_test.dart:976-978` ("Pin the registry poll table: the fake pid stays verifiably alive on every host"): `cli.shellJobsRegistryForTest.livenessTableOverride = () async => (pids: {4242, 4243}, starts: {})`. Presence-only rows (empty start map) keep the entries running forever per the #478 rule, so no late settle chain can ever fire; no product code changes. Reproduction is deterministic: a new test drives `adoptedPollTickForTest()` in-body — pre-fix it observes the fabricated pid settled off the real `ps` table (manifest rewritten empty post-body), post-fix the entry survives.

**Previous attempt**: None — first fix for this ticket.

# gh-2430 — [ci-red] v1.0.779 failed

### Root Cause

One real failure cascaded into all three red jobs. `Hostile ambient env` failed on `test/cli/agent_cli_waiting_fast_settle_test.dart` AC1: the teardown delete threw `Directory not empty (errno 39)`. The file's `settleCli()` fabricates adopted jobs with fake pids (4242/4243) but pins only the waiting layer's process probe — the registry's adopted-liveness poll (5 s wall-clock timer, `ShellJobRegistry._adopt`) still probed the REAL `ps` table. The tick always fires after the test body ends; finding no pid 4242, it settles the fabricated job and the `unawaited(jobSettled)` chain rewrites `running.json` in the temp workspace — under load inside the teardown delete (errno 39), outside it a resurrected deleted `/tmp` dir. `Quality gate` only failed because it aggregates `hostile-env = failure`; `Advance vpinned marker` failed with `E_PIN_PROVENANCE_MISSING` because publish (and its `SHA256SUMS`) is gated on the same gate's `dart_ok`. No product-code defect.

### Fix

- `test/cli/agent_cli_waiting_fast_settle_test.dart`: pin the registry poll table in `settleCli()` — `cli.shellJobsRegistryForTest.livenessTableOverride = () async => (pids: {4242, 4243}, starts: {})` — the same pattern already used in `agent_cli_waiting_integration_test.dart:976`. Presence-only rows keep the fabricated pids verifiably alive on every host (#478 rule), so no late settle chain can ever fire.
- Same file: added a deterministic regression test that drives `adoptedPollTickForTest()` in-body — pre-fix it observes the fabricated pid settled off the real `ps` table (manifest rewritten after the body), post-fix the entry survives.

### Test Coverage

- `REGRESSION (gh-2430 …)` — RED without the pin (`Expected: ['sh-gh2430'] / Actual: []`), GREEN with it.
- File suite: 4/4 passed, also under the hostile ambient env vars the CI leg exports.
- Full gate suite: see Notes — `dart test --exclude-tags integration` (the hostile-env leg's exact command).

### Notes

- Test-only change; no product code touched.
- `Quality gate` and `Advance vpinned marker` need no code fix: the marker advance self-heals on the next green run (publish attaches the signed `SHA256SUMS`, then `pin_release.sh v1.0.779` passes its provenance gate).
- Follow-up (not this ticket): `agent_cli_waiting_manifest_lock_test.dart` adopts fabricated pids with the same un-pinned poll; its `_deleteBestEffort` retry keeps it green but the identical one-line pin would remove the latent late-writer there too.

All verification complete. Final summary:

## gh-2430 — [ci-red] v1.0.779: fixed

**Root cause (one defect, two cascades).** The `Hostile ambient env` leg failed on `test/cli/agent_cli_waiting_fast_settle_test.dart` AC1: teardown threw `Directory not empty (errno 39)`. The fixture fabricates adopted jobs with fake pids (4242/4243) but pins only the waiting layer's probe — the registry's adopted-liveness poll (5 s wall-clock timer armed by `_adopt`) kept probing the **real** `ps` table. The tick always fires past the body end, settles the fabricated job, and the `unawaited(jobSettled)` chain rewrites `running.json` in the temp workspace — under CI load inside the teardown delete (errno 39); outside it, it silently resurrects the deleted `/tmp` dir. `Quality gate` failed only by aggregation (`hostile-env = failure`); `Advance vpinned marker` failed with `E_PIN_PROVENANCE_MISSING` because publish + `SHA256SUMS` are gated on the same gate's `dart_ok`. No product-code defect.

**Fix (test-only, root cause).** Pin the registry poll table in `settleCli()` — `livenessTableOverride = () async => (pids: {4242, 4243}, starts: {})` (presence-only rows keep the pids verifiably alive per the #478 rule) — the exact pattern `agent_cli_waiting_integration_test.dart:976` already established. Added a deterministic regression test driving `adoptedPollTickForTest()` in-body: verified **RED without the pin** (`Expected: ['sh-gh2430'] / Actual: []`), **GREEN with it**. Committed on `ai/gh-2430` at `f3b6479`; `outputs/gh-2430/{rca.md,response.md,scope_estimate.json}` written; no integration concerns (test-only change).

One flagged follow-up (documented in response.md Notes, intentionally NOT fixed here per minimum-fix discipline): `agent_cli_waiting_manifest_lock_test.dart` shares the un-pinned fabricated-pid pattern; its `_deleteBestEffort` retry keeps it green, but the same one-line pin would remove its latent late-writer.
